title: GTM Healthcare Intelligence
subtitle: Data provenance and query completeness
label: Self-initiated · review of my own demo
author: Kristen Martino
summary: The combined-quota fix passed three follow-up checks on October 26. Source disclosure and quarterly ranking were verified in the original October 25 review. The written-amount finding retains its original evidence and awaits a separate recheck.
provenance: This is a self-initiated review of a demo I own. It is not client work, independent assurance, or evidence of business impact. All sales and practice records used here are synthetic.
scope: Public GTM demo and portfolio data disclosures.
Selected source snapshots and recorded before-fix responses.
Five targeted requests to the production query endpoints.
Expected numbers recalculated directly from fixture rows without the query engine.
limits: The requests were purpose-selected; they are not a random sample or a model-accuracy benchmark.
This review did not test every query, security controls, production scale, or source accuracy.

The original before/after strings and five check results are October 25 records at d80dd7d. Only three quota follow-ups were rechecked October 26 at a1ce674; they do not establish the latest state of other findings.

No app code was changed or deployed for the assessment or quota recheck. The disclosure and quarterly-ranking repairs predated the original review; the quota fix was already deployed before the October 26 follow-up. The written-amount finding was not rechecked.
No user study, patient-data review, clinical validation or measured commercial outcome is claimed.
methodNote: AI tools supported implementation, testing and analysis. Numerical expectations were recomputed from the synthetic input records; this is not an independent third-party audit.

priorities.meaning: A published claim can give a materially wrong impression of the data in the example.
The requested task is incomplete or unnecessarily blocked. Scope is this demo, not a clinical severity rating.

findings.title: The public-data label was broader than the shipped snapshot.
findings.risk: A reader could infer that the displayed provider counts came from a completed CMS import. This is a review risk; no user misunderstanding was measured.
findings.observation: The earlier project summary described “synthetic and public data” beside a “CMS NPPES · Medicare PUF · Census” badge. The recorded SpectrumIQ input modes were synthetic providers and embedded demographic references.
findings.before:
…using synthetic and public data.
CMS NPPES · Medicare PUF · Census
findings.after:
Synthetic demo records.
Embedded references.
Optional public-data ingestion.
findings.fix: Publish separate disclosures for generated records, bundled references and the optional local-file loader. Avoid using a source name as evidence that ingestion occurred.
findings.verification: Verified on the public case-study page. All three labels are present and agree with the recorded input modes. Publication correction 43bdf1b; no data or calculation change is claimed.
acceptance: Display the three data paths distinctly.
Name the default snapshot’s actual input modes.
Describe public-file ingestion as optional, not a completed live import.

findings.title: Combined-quota output passed a dated follow-up.
findings.risk: The original response supplied correct individual figures but omitted the requested combined result. Without a total, a reader had to reconstruct weighted attainment from the amounts.
findings.observation: The combined-quota question returned only Chen and Kim rows on October 25. Three October 26 follow-up requests verified the combined total, individual quota rows and both together.
findings.question: What is the combined quota and attainment for Sarah Chen and David Kim in Q1 2025?
findings.before:
Chen: $504,000 bookings / $450,000 quota / 112.0%
Kim: $250,000 bookings / $350,000 quota / 71.4%
No combined result.
findings.after:
Fresh production response: the same two rep rows.
No combined quota, bookings or attainment was returned.
findings.fix: The existing fix returns a combined quota row and calculates attainment from summed bookings and quota, while preserving per-rep results. Fix 65e1db5 was already deployed before the follow-up; no app code was changed or deployed for this recheck.
findings.verification: Verified October 26 at serving revision a1ce674. Combined bookings $754,000 / quota $800,000 gives 94.25% attainment (94.3% displayed). Combined-only, per-rep-only and both-together requests matched expected quota rows. The per-rep-only response also contains a duplicate bookings-only block, retained in the raw packet.
acceptance: Return one combined result with $800,000 quota and $754,000 bookings.
Calculate attainment as 754,000 ÷ 800,000 = 94.25% (94.3% at one decimal).
Preserve correct per-rep results and supported cohort restrictions.

followUp.summary: Combined-only, per-rep-only and both-together requests passed the dated quota recheck.

findings.title: A valid quarterly ranking was rejected by the scope guard.
findings.risk: A supported question could be blocked even when the supplied tool queries covered the requested year. The observed failure was a clarification, not an incorrect number.
findings.observation: A recorded production response rejected an annual quarterly ranking. PR #22 changed coverage checks to accept valid period partitions per measure.
findings.question: Who had the most denials in each quarter of 2025?
findings.before: The shared period must apply to every independent measure.
findings.after:
Q1: Brooks — 81
Q2: Singh — 74
Q3: Brooks — 65
Q4: Yamamoto — 60
findings.fix: Accept complete quarterly partitions without accepting missing periods, swapped ranges or unsupported cohort links. This repair was implemented before the current assessment.
findings.verification: One fresh production request returned all four expected winners and counts. Expected values were recalculated directly from monthly fixture rows. This is a targeted recheck, not proof of every possible phrasing or tool plan.
acceptance: Return all four requested quarters with their own winners.
Continue rejecting genuinely incomplete or unsupported scopes.

findings.title: A written decimal threshold is safely rejected.
findings.risk: A supported numeric comparison becomes unusable when the amount is written in words. The guard prevents a misleading partial-number answer.
findings.observation: “At least one point five million” asks for clarification. The equivalent “at least $1.5M” query succeeds and selects Singh. Both behaviors were rechecked.
findings.question: Which providers had at least one point five million in revenue in 2025?
findings.before: The numeric threshold was not preserved. Please clarify the comparison; no calculation was run.
findings.after:
Written amount: clarification again.
Numeric control (≥ $1.5M): Singh — $1,592,362.
findings.fix: Parse the complete written quantity and scale, or offer an explicit numeric rephrasing. Keep the existing stop behavior when the full amount cannot be preserved.
findings.verification: Open at the tested revision. No incorrect numerical answer was returned for the written version. The direct annual revenue sums confirm the numeric-control result.
acceptance: Interpret one point five million as 1,500,000, or clearly ask for the supported numeric form.
Match the $1.5M control when calculation proceeds.
Never silently accept only the leading “one.”

plan.title: Retain combined and per-rep regression checks
plan.text: Preserve the total, individual rows and both-together behavior. Keep attainment weighted by summed bookings and quota; retain the scenario tests covering all 63 nonempty rep subsets.

plan.title: Recheck the written-amount finding separately
plan.text: Re-run the original written and numeric forms before determining whether any limitation remains. Retain the stop when the complete amount or a required input is missing.

plan.title: Retain the provenance and period checks
plan.text: Keep the three data disclosures and quarterly coverage checks. These findings were verified in the original review, not in the October 26 quota follow-up.

futureOpportunity.title: A separate enhancement: one reconciled public-data slice
futureOpportunity.text: A small NPPES/Census ingestion run with source vintage, transformations and reconciliation would demonstrate the optional loader. This is an expansion opportunity, not a defect in a demo that deliberately uses synthetic data.

hiringNarrative.label: Self-initiated review of my own demo
hiringNarrative.title: Combined quota fix verified
hiringNarrative.opening: The October 25 check returned correct rep figures but omitted their combined total. An October 26 recheck confirms combined bookings, quota and weighted attainment, with individual results retained.

decisions.title: Combined and individual results verified
paragraphs: Combined-only, per-rep-only and both-together requests were checked. Combined attainment uses total bookings divided by total quota, rather than averaging rep percentages.

decisions.title: Source labels corrected
paragraphs: Public labels named CMS sources. The snapshot used synthetic provider records and embedded demographic references. Corrected wording distinguishes both from optional public-file ingestion; the wording repair changed no data or calculations.

decisions.title: Written amount not rechecked
paragraphs: On October 25, “one point five million” required clarification; “$1.5M” returned Singh at $1,592,362. The no-show calculation stopped without the required appointment count. These observations were not rechecked on October 26.

verification: The original five questions used synthetic sample records; expected answers were calculated separately from the app. Source disclosures and all four quarterly winners were verified then.

Three quota follow-ups on October 26 checked an existing deployed fix. No app code changed for the recheck. Forty-five JavaScript tests passed, covering all 63 nonempty rep subsets. This is not overall model accuracy.
hiringNarrative.next: Retain quota and per-rep regression checks. Recheck the written-amount finding separately before deciding whether another fix is needed.
